legend: Sporadic nodular adrenocortical disease with a nodule measuring 7 mm. With the exception of its size (< 10 mm), sporadic nodular adrenocortical disease is indistinguishable from other non-functioning adenomas.

This is the most common form of bilateral micronodular adrenocortical disease. It is characterized by multiple pigmented small nodules (< 10 mm) that often range in size from 1 to 4 mm. Cortical micronodules are enriched in compact (lipid-poor) adrenocortical cells. Internodular cortical atrophy with reduced cortical thickness can be noted.

The disease is characterized by bilateral multiple clear cell–rich nodules, each measuring > 10 mm.
Gross examination of primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease identifies bilateral small pigmented cortical nodules (< 10 mm, often < 5 mm).
Irregular left adrenal gland enlargement due to multiple adrenal cortical nodules, each > 10 mm.
Irregular right adrenal gland enlargement due to multiple adrenal cortical nodules, each > 10 mm.

Two foci of randomly distributed sporadic nodular adrenocortical disease that ranged in size from 1.5 to 3 mm are seen. The large focus is enriched in compact cells with variable pigment deposition, whereas the small focus is enriched in lipid-rich clear cells.

This patient had bilateral cortical micronodules, identified as compact (lipid-poor) adrenocortical cells within the zona fasciculata and zona reticularis. They are only millimeters in size.
